The IVM-MR analysis showed a casual association between genetically predicted circulating levels of interleukin-16 and both ALM and grip strength (ALM: OR = 0.990, 95% CI: 0.980-1.000, p = .049; grip strength: OR = 0.971, 95% CI: 0.948-0.995, p = .020). Comparable results were confirmed via the MR-Egger, Weighted Median, Weighted Mode, and Simple Mode methods.

The primary MR analysis using the IVW method reveals a significant negative correlation between Metallothionein-1F (MT-1F), zinc finger protein 134 (ZNF134), calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase type 1D (CAMK1D), and EF-hand calcium-binding domain-containing protein 14 (EFCAB14) with the occurrence of osteoarthritis (OA) (p value < 0.05). Notably, even in combined models accounting for confounding factors, the negative association between these four MPs and OA remained significant.

Three immune factors demonstrated protective associations: C-C motif chemokine 4 (OR: 0.682, 95% CI: 0.509–0.915, p = 0.011), leukemia inhibitory factor receptor (OR: 0.588, 95% CI: 0.374–0.924, p = 0.021), and macrophage inflammatory protein (OR: 0.521, 95% CI: 0.345–0.786, p = 0.002). These findings were consistent across multiple analytical approaches and cancer types, including cervical cancer and bone/articular cartilage malignancies.

We applied two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), summary-data-based MR, and Bayesian colocalization to evaluate the associations of genetically proxied levels of 213 lipid-lowering drug target proteins with lumbar spinal stenosis risk. Results MR identified three proteins increasing disease risk, with placental alkaline phosphatase (ALPP) consistently replicating across platforms (colocalization at rs12478529, PP.H4 = 0.9979).
